w: Named for crucible steel -- the process invented in Sheffield in 1740 that built the city's industrial fortune -- this 1971 theatre has hosted the World Snooker Championship every year since 1977. The Guardian calls it the spiritual home of snooker. An industrial name doing a very different kind of work now.
s: Named for steel, famous for snooker
_facts: Opened 1971; named for crucible steel, developed in Sheffield in 1740
Has hosted the World Snooker Championship annually since 1977
The Guardian has called it the 'spiritual home of snooker'
Also hosts the World Women's Snooker Championship and World Seniors Championship

w: Known as much by its street as by its name -- the Wolseley Road Mosque, or Madina Masjid -- this was the first mosque built in Sheffield from the ground up for the purpose, rather than converted from something else. A modest building with a genuine first to its name.
_facts: Also known as Madina Masjid or the Wolseley Road Mosque
The first purpose-built mosque in Sheffield
